_note: Illustrative FMEA for a turbofan engine, built for a learning demo from C-MAPSS sensor documentation. Not OEM maintenance data.

modes.name: HPC efficiency loss (blade fouling / erosion)
modes.effect: Higher gas-path temperatures and fuel flow; reduced thrust and EGT margin.
actions: Review the T30/T50 and Ps30 trends to confirm a gradual efficiency loss, not a step change
Perform an on-wing HPC compressor wash
Re-check the health index over the next 10 cycles; recovery confirms fouling
If no recovery, schedule an HPC borescope inspection for erosion

modes.name: HPC flow capacity loss
modes.effect: Reduced surge margin with risk of compressor stall; loss of pressure ratio.
causes: Blade damage or excessive tip clearance
actions: Restrict the engine to reduced-power operation until inspected
Perform an HPC borescope inspection (stages 1-9) for blade damage and tip rub
Check variable stator vane rigging and actuator
Plan HPC module removal if damage exceeds manual limits

modes.name: HPT blade thermal wear
modes.effect: Rising exhaust temperature and loss of turbine efficiency.
actions: Trend EGT margin (T50) against core speed
Perform an HPT borescope inspection for coating loss and burn-through
Inspect cooling air bleed lines for restriction

modes.name: Fan blade damage (foreign object)
modes.effect: Vibration and thrust loss; possible imbalance.
actions: Visually inspect fan blades for nicks, dents and leading-edge damage
Blend or replace damaged blades per manual limits

modes.name: Sensor drift or failure
actions: Cross-check the deviating sensor against physically related sensors
Inspect the probe, wiring and connector
Replace or recalibrate the sensor, then confirm readings return to baseline
